subject: Reasoning
topic: Logic Puzzles — Tabular and Conditional Deduction

questions.stem: Five friends — A, B, C, D, E — are seated in a row facing north. A is to the left of B. C is to the right of D. E is at the rightmost end. D is to the left of A. Who is in the middle?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Constraints: D < A (D left of A), A < B (A left of B), D < C (C right of D), E = rightmost. A valid arrangement: D, A, B, C, E (left to right). Verify: D<A ✓, A<B ✓, D<C ✓, E is rightmost ✓. Middle (3rd position) = B.

questions.stem: P, Q, R, S are four friends. P is taller than Q. R is shorter than S. Q is taller than S. Who is the tallest?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Chain: P > Q (given), Q > S (given), S > R (given). So: P > Q > S > R. P is the tallest, R is the shortest.

questions.stem: In a class, there are 5 students — Anil, Bina, Charu, Dev, and Esha. Each studies a different subject: Maths, Science, English, History, Geography. Anil does not study Maths or Science. Bina studies English. Charu studies History. Dev does not study Geography. Which subject does Anil study?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Known: Bina=English, Charu=History. Remaining: Anil, Dev, Esha get Maths, Science, Geography. Anil ≠ Maths, Anil ≠ Science → Anil = Geography. Dev ≠ Geography (already taken) → Dev has Maths or Science. Esha gets the remaining one.

questions.stem: Six people — I, J, K, L, M, N — sit in a circle facing the centre. K sits opposite L. I sits to the immediate right of K. M sits to the immediate left of L. J and N are adjacent. Who sits opposite I?
questions.explanation: B is correct. In a 6-seat circle, opposite seats are 3 apart. K opposite L; I immediately right of K; M immediately left of L. Arrange: ...K, I, ?, L, M, ?... (circle). Since K opposite L (3 apart), I (1 right of K) is 3 apart from M (1 left of L). So I opposite M.

questions.stem: A, B, C, D, E work in different departments: HR, IT, Finance, Marketing, Legal. A works in IT. C does not work in HR or Finance. D works in Marketing. E does not work in Legal. Which department does E work in?

options.option_text: Cannot be uniquely determined from the given information

questions.explanation: D is correct. Deductions: A=IT, D=Marketing, C=Legal (since C≠HR, C≠Finance → C must be Legal). Remaining departments: HR and Finance for B and E. Constraint 'E ≠ Legal' is already satisfied (C has Legal). No further constraint distinguishes B from E for HR vs Finance → cannot be uniquely determined. This tests whether students over-deduce.

questions.stem: In a row of 8 students facing north, Priya is 5th from the left and Sunita is 3rd from the right. How many students are between Priya and Sunita?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Sunita is 3rd from the right in a row of 8 → her position from the left = 8 − 3 + 1 = 6th. Priya is 5th from left. Positions 5 and 6 are adjacent → 0 students between them.

questions.stem: Three friends Ravi, Suresh, and Tarun each own a different pet: a cat, a dog, and a fish. Ravi does not own the dog. Suresh does not own the cat. Tarun owns the fish. Who owns the cat?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Tarun=fish (given). Suresh≠cat → Suresh gets dog. Ravi≠dog (already Suresh has dog) → Ravi gets cat. Final: Ravi=cat, Suresh=dog, Tarun=fish.

questions.stem: Mohan walks 4 km east, then 3 km north, then 4 km west. How far is he from his starting point and in which direction?
questions.explanation: B is correct. East 4 km then West 4 km = net 0 horizontal. North 3 km = net 3 km north. Final position = 3 km directly north of start. Direction puzzles: always track net x (E-W) and net y (N-S) displacements separately.

questions.stem: A person starts from point X, walks 5 km south, then 12 km east. What is the straight-line distance from X to the final point?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Moving 5 km south then 12 km east creates a right angle. Straight-line distance = √(5² + 12²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13 km. Pythagorean triple: 5-12-13 — memorise this and other common triples (3-4-5, 8-15-17) for direction problems.

questions.stem: Six boxes are stacked one on top of another. Box A is above Box B. Box C is below Box D. Box B is below Box C. Box E is at the top. Box F is at the bottom. What is the order from top to bottom?

options.option_text: E, A, B, C, D, F
E, A, B, D, C, F
E, D, C, A, B, F
E, A, D, C, B, F

questions.explanation: D is correct. Given: A > B (A above B), D > C (D above C), C > B (B below C), E = top, F = bottom. Chain: B < C < D and B < A. Since there are 6 boxes total, A and D compete for spots 2 and 3 above B. A is above B but no constraint between A and D/C → most consistent order placing A above D: E, A, D, C, B, F (top to bottom).
